question: For constant M_c and a1_eff(a,k)=k_com^2/(a^2 M_c^2+k_com^2), what exact condition allows simultaneous cosmological compensation over a declared history a>=a_min,k<=k_cos_max and local family-I recovery at k_local?
tolerance: 0<epsilon<1/2; cosmology requires a1_eff<=epsilon, local recovery requires a1_eff>=1-epsilon
target_identities: cosmology over a>=a_min,k<=k_cos_max requires M_c^2 >= ((1-epsilon)/epsilon) k_cos_max^2/a_min^2
a constant-M_c window exists iff k_local/(k_cos_max/a_min) >= (1-epsilon)/epsilon
for epsilon=0.01 the ratio threshold is exactly 99
for fixed nonzero k_com, a1_eff->1 as a->0, so no finite constant M_c can maintain cosmological compensation to arbitrarily early a
non_claims: does not select a_min; the EFT starting epoch must be physically declared
does not identify k_local with a particular Solar-System experiment
does not prove that a1_eff<=epsilon is sufficient to keep the full cosmological likelihood within epsilon
does not exclude time/state-dependent M_c or a different auxiliary operator
does not implement the completion in CLASS
next_gate_if_pass: audit the actual production CLASS integration/source history to freeze a physically relevant a_min and k_cos_max, then test whether a constant-M_c interval survives before implementing the completion
